findings.title: Dry runs can write through copied symlinks
findings.description: `verbatimSymlinks: true` preserves links into the real filesystem. If `.claude/rules` links to an absolute directory, the sandbox installer follows that link and writes new rules there. A symlinked `.context-forge` can similarly expose real manifests to writes. Reject or safely isolate symlinks before installing, and add regression tests proving dry runs leave linked destinations unchanged.

findings.title: Native worktree pruning lacks containment checks
findings.description: Worktrees now use `InstallManifest.finish()`, which joins manifest paths directly to the checkout root and deletes matching files (`manifest.ts:188-193`). A manifest entry containing `../outside.md` and its matching checksum can therefore delete a file outside the worktree; symlinked parent directories also escape containment. Restore lexical and real-path containment checks from the removed pruning implementation, with corresponding safety tests.

findings.title: Agents dry-run previews generate different rule references
findings.description: Changing `targetRoot` to the sandbox while retaining the original guide path changes generated `AGENTS.md` content. `scopedRuleIndex()` computes references relative to `targetRoot`, so a real install emits project-relative references while its preview emits absolute guide paths. Consequently, an unchanged agents installation reports a spurious modification. Separate logical output paths from sandbox write paths, and test agents dry-run idempotency.
